caption: Figure 2: The two plots on the left show average reward per episode on Breakout and Seaquest respectively during training. The statistics were computed by running an ϵ -greedy policy with ϵ = 0 . 05 for 10000 steps. The two plots on the right show the average maximum predicted action-value of a held out set of states on Breakout and Seaquest respectively. One epoch corresponds to 50000 minibatch weight updates or roughly 30 minutes of training time.
description:
Figure: Four line plots showing training progress over epochs. Left two plots: "Average Reward per Episode" on Breakout and Seaquest. Right two plots: "Average Q" on Breakout and Seaquest. Breakout plots show higher average rewards and Q values compared to Seaquest. Breakout's average reward peaks at around 250, while Seaquest's peaks at around 1800. Breakout's average Q value peaks at around 4, while Seaquest's peaks at around 8.

caption: Figure 3: The leftmost plot shows the predicted value function for a 30 frame segment of the game Seaquest. The three screenshots correspond to the frames labeled by A, B, and C respectively.
description:

Screenshots: Correspond to frames labeled A, B, and C.
Text: Frame #, Value Function, OXYGEN, ACTIVATION.

Description: The figure shows a plot of the predicted value function for a 30 frame segment of the game Seaquest, along with three screenshots corresponding to specific frames labeled A, B, and C. The screenshots provide visual context for the frames, showing the game's state at those points.
